styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Laneways, markets and the old city grid.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Coffee, laneway bars and market grazing.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Beaches, gardens and the bay foreshore.

stays.why: Walk to the laneways, Queen Victoria Market and the free tram zone. Best base for a first visit.
River views and a short walk over the bridge to the CBD. Good for evenings out.
Beach, pier and cake shops. A tram ride from the centre; quieter at night.
Bars, galleries and cafés on Brunswick Street. Walkable and lively.

food: Start with coffee: Melbourne cafés take it seriously. A flat white is the local order, about $4–6.
Queen Victoria Market: graze the deli hall and hot-doughnut stall. Cheapest on a weekday morning.
Laneway bars and small restaurants fill the CBD blocks off Flinders Lane. Book dinner on weekends.
Try a pub counter meal (parma or pie) for a filling lunch, roughly $20–30.
Asian food is strong and cheap: dumplings and noodles in Chinatown and Richmond, about $12–20 a plate.
more_time: Swap a city day for the Great Ocean Road: a long day tour, or drive yourself and stay a night in Apollo Bay.
Take a train to the Yarra Valley or Mornington Peninsula for wineries; check timetables and book tastings.
Phillip Island for penguins at dusk: tours run from the city, or drive about 2 hours. Book ahead.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the laneways, markets and galleries, with a day left for the beach or a wine trip.

month_notes: January: warm and mostly dry, highs near 26°C. Book accommodation early; it's peak holiday season.
February: similar to January, highs near 26°C, few rain days. Good for the beach and outdoor dining.
March: still warm at 24°C, a little more rain. Comfortable for walking the city.
April: cooler at 20°C with about 9 rain days. Pack a light jacket.
May: cool and wetter, highs near 16°C and 11 rain days. Plan indoor sights and cafés.
June: cold, highs near 14°C, about 10 rain days. Bring warm layers.
July: the coldest month, highs near 13°C and the most rain (13 days). Expect grey, damp days.
August: cold like July, highs near 14°C, 12 rain days. Rug up for the beach and gardens.
September: warming to 17°C but still wet, 12 rain days. Carry an umbrella.
October: mild at 20°C, 12 rain days. Good for markets and day trips between showers.
November: pleasant at 22°C, 11 rain days. A strong month for the city and coast.
December: warm at 25°C, 9 rain days. Festive and busy; book ahead.

climate_guide.summary: Temperate and changeable: warm dry summers, cool wet winters, and rain possible in any month.

items.title: Best time: December to March
items.text: Warm days around 24–26°C and fewer rain days. Ideal for the beach, gardens and outdoor dining.

items.title: Winter is cool and damp (June to August)
items.text: Highs only 13–14°C with 10–13 rain days a month. Bring a warm coat and plan indoor sights.

items.title: Rain in every month
items.text: Expect 6–13 rain days whatever the season. Carry a small umbrella and a light layer.

items.title: Weather changes fast
items.text: A warm morning can turn cool and showery by afternoon. Dress in layers you can add or shed.

items.title: Beach days are summer-only
items.text: St Kilda and the bay are best December to March. Water stays cool even then.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for walking. Add a hat and sunscreen for summer.

transit.best: Trams in the CBD and trains for longer hops; walk the grid for short trips.

modes.text: Trains run every 10–20 minutes and reach the suburbs. A Night Network runs after midnight on Fri–Sat.
Trams are free inside the CBD Free Tram Zone. Touch on with myki only if you travel beyond it.
Buses fill the gaps where trains and trams don't go. Pay with myki.
Taxis are metered; Uber, DiDi and Ola operate and often cost less. Handy for late nights.
Easy on freeways but CBD parking is costly. Skip the car in town; rent only for day trips.
The CBD grid is walkable. Shared bikes and scooters cover short hops.
